note: CR-38.2 / CR-38.3 (Florian 2026-09-15) with design directive F-98: per-benchmark caveat metadata. Two blocks. `judged` names the benchmarks whose score is set by a human vote or by a judge model's opinion rather than by a verifiable ground truth (unit tests, an answer key, a backend state check, a deterministic pattern count); those rows carry the `Judged` tag and never average with task-accuracy rows inside one category composite. `freshness` records what the verified source itself states about the task/question date window and about contamination control; where the source states nothing, the field stays null and says so — nothing here is inferred. The `saturated` flag of CR-38.2 is NOT curated here: it is computed from the results we hold (see `saturationOf` in lib/benchmark-matrix.mjs), so it can never drift away from the data on the page. Keys are benchmark family keys (the registry id before '::') or, for axes without a registry entry, the taxonomy key.
quote_rule: Every entry carries a `quote` that must appear verbatim in the named field of the benchmark's own registry entry (data/raw/benchmarks/registry.json) or, for non-registry axes, in data/benchmark-taxonomy.json. test/benchmark-caveats.test.mjs enforces this, so a classification can never rest on a sentence no source wrote.

review.result: 31 of 32 rows agreed. One disagreement, accepted and applied: swe-atlas-test-writing -> judged, because its own description names LLM judges as the graders, which its two sibling boards do not. No other change.

judged_definition: The published number ranks or rates outputs by preference or quality. A judge model that only checks whether an answer is correct (an equality checker, a majority vote on accuracy, an LLM normaliser in front of exact matching) is NOT judged — the ground truth still decides.

considered_not_judged.lisanbench: Chains are validated programmatically against a pinned dictionary (edit distance 1, no repeats); no judge model.
